1.

The petitioner aged about 32 years has sought compensation to the tune of Rs. 15,00,000/ with
interest @ 12 % per annum from the date of filing of petition till the date of realization, for the
injuries sustained by him in a Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 23.03.2015 at about
8:00 Pm near Cng Petrol Pump, Bahalgarh Road, Sonipat, Haryana, involving Auto Rickshaw
bearing registration no. Hr69B1979 (offending vehicle) being driven by respondent no. 1 in a rash
and negligent manner.

2. It is averred in the claim petition that on 23.03.2015, the petitioner was going to government
hospital through offending vehicle.

At about 8:00 Pm, when the offending vehicle reached in front
of Cng Petrol Pump, it rashly and negligently took a sharp turn at a very high speed, due to which it
turned turtle, as a result of which, he sustained grievous injuries.

He was immediately taken to Lok
Nayak Hospital, Delhi by one Mr. Anuj.

Fir No. 161/15, u/s. 279/337 Ipc was registered at Ps.
Sonipat Sadar with Macp No. 5937/16; Fir No. 161/15 Dod: 19.04.2023 regard to the said
accident.

The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with
respondent no. 3/Shriram General Insurance Company Limited during the period in question.

3. In his written statement, the respondent no. 1 i.e. driver raised preliminary objection that the
accident had not taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.

He
claimed that he was having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.

On merits, he
has denied the averments made in the claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.

4. In his written statement, the respondent no. 2 i.e. registered owner raised preliminary objection
that he was not the owner of offending vehicle at the time of accident as he had already transferred
the Rc of the offending vehicle in the name of respondent no. 1.

On merits, he has denied the
averments made in the claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.

5. In its written statement, the respondent no. 3/insurance company raised preliminary objection
that the respondent no. 1 was carrying excess passengers against the carrying capacity of offending
vehicle i.e. 4 persons including driver at the time of accident and thus, there was a violation of terms
and conditions of insurance policy and it has been claimed that it is not liable to pay any
compensation to the petitioner.
Macp No. 5937/16; Fir No. 161/15 Dod: 19.04.2023

However, it has admitted that offending
vehicle was insured with it at the time of accident.

On merits, it has denied the averments made in
the claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.

6. From the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed vide order dated 02.05.2017
passed by my Ld. Predecessor:
1.

Whether the injured Amit Dimri suffered injuries in road traffic accident on 23.03.2015 at 8:00
pm at Cng Petrol Pump, Bahalgarh Road, Spt, Sonepat, Haryana, within the jurisdiction of Ps.
Sonepat Sadar, Haryana

due to rashness and negligence on the part of Mehar Singh/R1, who was
driving Auto Rickshaw bearing registration no. Hr69B1979, owned by Sh. Mukesh/R2 and
insured with Shriram General Insurance Co Ltd/R 3?

My findings on the issues are as under:
10.

sentences.text: During his cross examination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that 34 persons including driver respondent no. 1 were travelling in the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

He further deposed that three persons were sitting on the rear portion and he alongwith respondent no.
1 were sitting on the driver seat of offending vehicle at the time of accident.

He further deposed that since, he fell unconscious due to the impact of the accident, it was not within his knowledge if any other person sitting in offending vehicle, had also sustained injuries or not.
He denied the suggestion that there was no negligence on the part of respondent no. 1.
He further denied the suggestion that he was sitting as unauthorized passenger on the offending vehicle.
12. It is evident from the testimony of PW1 that respondents could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of crossexamination.
Said witness is found to have successfully withstood the test of cross examination.
Even otherwise, PW1 himself is the injured having sustained injuries due to the accident in question.
There is no reason as to why he would depose falsely against respondent no.1.
Furthermore, it is an undisputed fact that FIR No.161/15 u/s 279/337 IPC
was registered at PS.
MACP No. 5937/16; FIR No. 161/15 DOD: 19.04.2023 Sonepat Sadar with regard to accident in question.
Copy of said FIR (Ex. PW1/B), would show that same was registered on the statement of complainant Sh. Surender on the date of accident itself i.e. 23.03.2015.
The contents of said FIR would show that the said complainant had disclosed the same sequence of facts leading to the accident, as deposed by PW1 during the course of inquiry.
The registration number of offending vehicle to be TSR no. HR69B1979 is also disclosed therein.

The respondents no. 1 & 2 have failed to substantiate the plea that petitioner had any kind of ill will or enmity against them so as to falsely implicate respondent no. 1 in criminal case or to depose falsely against them during the course of inquiry.

13. The very fact that respondent no. 1 was chargesheeted(which is part of DAR) by the police for offences punishable u/s. 279/337/338 IPC would further show that Investigating Agency also concluded after completion of the investigation that accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by its driver(respondent no.1 herein) and same also points out towards the fact that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Hence, there is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 1 and/or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioner herein.

14. It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying MACP No. 5937/16; FIR No. 161/15 DOD: 19.04.2023 as to how and under what circumstances, the accident had taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.

15. Apart from above, copy of MLC (Ex. PW1/E) of injured prepared at Lok Nayak Hospital, New Delhi shows that he had been removed to said hospital on 23.03.2015 at about 11:12 pm with alleged history of RTA.
On his local examination, he was found to have sustained multiple injuries as mentioned therein.
The said injuries are consistent with the injuries which are sustained in a motor vehicular accident.
Again, there is no challenge to the said document from the side of respondents including insurance company.

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove on the basis of pre ponderence of probabilities that he had sustained grievous injuries in road accident which took place on 23.03.2015 at about 8:00 PM, near CNG Petrol Pump, Bahalgarh Road, Sonipat, Haryana, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Thus, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly.
MEDICAL
EXPENSES

18. The petitioner has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex. PW1/X) that after the accident, he had been taken to Lok Nayak Hospital, Delhi and thereafter, he was shifted to Fortis Hospital, Shalimar Bagh, Delhi.
He deposed that he had sustained grievous injury in the accident.
He has relied upon medical bills Ex. PW1/G colly.

During his crossexamination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that he was not having any mediclaim policy at the time of accident and he did not received reimbursement of any amount against the said medical bills.
He denied the suggestion that the medical bills and treatment record filed by him were forged and fabricated.
19. It is relevant to note that the injured has relied upon medical bills(Ex. PW1/3 colly) to the tune of Rs. 2,55,980/ only.
It is quite evident that the respondents have not disputed the authenticity and genuineness of the said medical bills during the course of inquiry.

They have also not led MACP No.
5937/16; FIR No. 161/15 DOD: 19.04.2023 any evidence in rebuttal so as to create any doubt on the genuineness of said bills.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs. 2,55,980/ is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
LOSS OF INCOME 20.

PW1 has categorically deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex PW1/X) that he had been working as Retail Manager in Ess Gee Trendz Pvt. Ltd and getting monthly salary of Rs. 50,350/ at the time of accident.
He further deposed that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he could not work for considerable period.

During his cross examination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that he had joined the services of the company after receipt of his appointment letter Ex. PW1/H and no separate acceptance of the appointment letter was given in writing by him.
He further deposed that his salary used to be paid by transferring the salary amount in his bank account.
He deposed that he had already filed the computerized copies of his pay slips for the months of January to March, 2015.
He deposed that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he could not attend his duty for a period of 3 months or so.

He further deposed that he Sh. Amit Dimri vs Sh. Mehar Singh on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2557438/

The medical treatment record i.e. Discharge Summary (which is part of Ex. PW1/E colly) of Lok Nayak Hospital, in respect of petitioner/injured, would reveal that he was admitted in the said hospital on 24.03.2015 and discharged on 31.03.2015.

As per the said record, the case of the petitioner was of RTA with blunt trauma abdomen and chest with right 9th to 12th rib fracture with L1 to L4 transverse process fracture with splenic laceration with pelvic fracture urethral injury .
22. The medical treatment record filed by the petitioner reveals that he had taken treatment from different hospitals i.e. from Lok Nayak Hospital, Fortis Hospital and Sir Ganga Ram Hospital etc.
It can not be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries as mentioned above due to the accident.

sentences.text: It may be noted here that as per document i.e. Appointment letter dated 04.04.2014 (Ex. PW1/H) and payslip of March 2015(which is part of Ex. PW1/K colly), petitioner was getting monthly salary of Rs. 47,850/ (excluding Rs. 2500/ on account of tax deducted at source).
After comparing the aforesaid documents, it is clear that petitioner was working in ESS GEE Trendz Pvt Ltd at the time of accident.

However, there is some difference in the monthly salary,
he used to receive at the time of accident and after the accident.

It is apparent on record that at the time of accident, petitioner was getting monthly salary of Rs. 47,850/(as per document Ex. PW1/K colly) and Rs. 38,000/ per month (as per document Ex. PW2/3 colly) in the month of March, 2016 i.e. after about one year of the accident.

A judicial notice can be taken of the salary record relied upon by the petitioner in the present case that after the accident, his performance might have been affected and due to that reason, his salary might have been reduced to Rs. 38,000/ per month from Rs. 47,850/ per month.
I am more concerned about the salary of relevant period i.e. salary which was being received by the petitioner at the time of accident.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, I am inclined to accept the monthly salary of petitioner as Rs. 47,850/.

Hence, a sum of Rs. 2,87,000/
(rounded off) (Rs. 47,850/ x 6) is awarded in favour of petitioner for loss of leaves.

Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the matter titled as " Vinod Kumar Bitoo Vs. Roshni & Ors."

entities.text: Vinod Kumar Bitoo Vs. Roshni & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: passed in appeal bearing no. MAC.APP 518/2010 decided on 05.07.12, has held as under: " It is difficult to measure the pain and suffering in terms of money which is suffered by a victim on account of serious injuries caused to him in a motor vehicle accident.

Since the compensation is required to be paid for pain and suffering an attempt must be made to award compensation which may have some objective relation with the pain and suffering underwent by the victim.

For this purpose, the Claims Tribunal and the Courts normally consider the nature of injury; the part of the body where the injuries were sustained, surgeries, if any, underwent by the victim, confinement in the hospital and the duration of treatment".
26.
The petitioner has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex PW1/X) that he had sustained grievous injuries in the accident in question.
Thus, he would have undergone great physical sufferings and mental shock on account of the accident in question.

Keeping in view the medical treatment record of petitioner available on record and the nature of injuries suffered by him, I hereby award a sum of Rs. 75,000/ towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.

MACP No. 5937/16; FIR No. 161/15 DOD: 19.04.2023 LOSS OF GENERAL AMENITIES &
ENJOYMENT OF LIFE 27.
As already mentioned above, there is sufficient evidence on record to establish that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries due to the accident.
Thus, he would not be able to enjoy general amenities of life after the accident in question and his quality of life has been definitely affected.

In view of the nature of injuries suffered by him, I award a notional sum of Rs. 75,000/
towards loss of general amenities and enjoyment of life to the petitioner.

sentences.text: During the course of arguments, Ld. Counsel for petitioners argued that petitioner had spent considerable amount on his special diet, conveyance and attendant.
It is relevant to note here that the petitioner has failed to lead any cogent evidence to prove the amount, if any spent on special diet, conveyance and attendant as aforesaid by him.
At the same time, it cannot be overlooked that petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.

Thus, he would have taken special rich protein diet for his speedy recovery and would have also incurred considerable amount towards conveyance charges while commuting to the concerned hospital as OPD patient for his regular check up & follow up during the period of his MACP No. 5937/16; FIR No. 161/15 DOD: 19.04.2023 medical treatment.
He would have been definitely helped by some person either outsider or from his family, to perform his daily activities as also while visiting the hospital during the course of his medical treatment.

In these facts and circumstances, I hereby award a notional sum of Rs. 10,000/
for special diet and Rs. 15,000/each for conveyance charges and attendant charges to the petitioner.

Thus, the total compensation is assessed as under:
1. Medical Expenses Rs. 2,55,980/
2. Loss of income Rs. 2,87,000/
3. Pain and suffering Rs. 75,000/
4. Loss of general amenities and Rs. 75,000/ enjoyment of life 5.

Conveyance, special diet & Rs. 40,000/ attendant charges Total Rs. 7,32,980/ Rounded off to Rs. 7,33,000/
29.
This brings me down to the next question as to who, out of the respondents, are liable to pay the compensation amount so assessed herein above.

Ld counsel for insurance company vehemently argued that petitioner was travelling in the offending vehicle as unauthorized person as the seating capacity of offending vehicle was 4 persons including driver and MACP No. 5937/16; FIR No. 161/15 DOD: 19.04.2023 the petitioner was the fifth passenger in the offending vehicle and thus, there is breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy.
Thus, insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
30. It is relevant to mention here that insurance company has failed to lead any cogent evidence in respect of its aforesaid plea as raised by it in its written statement.
In the absence of any cogent evidence, the aforesaid plea raised by the insurance company is rejected.
Keeping in view the existence of valid insurance policy, respondent no. 3/insurance company becomes liable to pay the compensation amount, as insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured.
Issue no. 2 is decided accordingly.
